We also expect the strong revenue growth and operating leverage to drive over 30% EPS growth. The stock looks attractively priced at 14x our forecast FY27 EPS. Buy.

| | **Optical and IP growth outlook likely to see upside:** Nokia has twice increased its guidance this year for Optical+IP growth, and we expect its initial 25-30% guidance for growth in 2027 to be similarly conservative. The upside in 2026 came mainly in IP Networks, following a switch design win at Google. The upside in 2027 is expected to come mainly from Optical Networks, on the back of the large starting backlog, strong order momentum and rising InP capacity at the San Jose fab. We forecast IP+Optical revenues to grow 31% next year, with Optical revenues growing 34%.**Operating leverage to drive up margins** : We model Network Infrastructure (NI) operating costs to grow 8% in 2027, slightly lower than the estimated 10% growth in 2026. With revenues growing much faster (JEFe 21.8%), we forecast the NI operating margin to rise from an estimated 11.5% in 2026 to 16.4% in 2027. The resulting 70% growth in NI operating income is modelled to drive a 42% increase in overall operating income. We expect strong NI revenue growth in 2028 to again drive earnings growth in that year. We raise our 2027 and 2028 EPS forecasts by 6% and 8% to €0.53 and €0.66 respectively. Our forecasts represent EPS growth of 31% CAGR over the next two years.**Fundamentals are likely to be more resilient, even if AI investment slows:** There are rising concerns on the strength of future AI data centre investments, due to constraints like financing and availability of power supply. However, Nokia's Scale Across growth in Optical is partly based on connecting existing data centres, rather than just new constructions. In a scenario of lower investments in new data centre builds, the need to increase compute capacity by Scaling Across existing data centres is likely to increase. Nokia is also gaining share in a number of product segments, which reduces its risk from an AI investment slowdown.**Valuations are attractive:** On our forecasts Nokia is trading at 14x and 11.3x FY27 and FY28 EPS. This is in-line with Ericsson's PERs of 14.3x and 13.1x for 2027 and 2028, respectively. It is also broadly in-line with Nokia's trading range prior to its AI-related revenue acceleration from Q4-25. Our FY27 and FY28 EPS forecasts are over 20% above consensus and we expect market estimates to move up. We see limited scope for further de-rating, and believe the stock is attractively priced. We expect the market to once again re-rate the stock above its historical valuation range, given its accelerating revenue and earnings growth rates.

Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * Capex now materializes in supply adds in two years, more heads and media needed to just keep up with demand
  * Pricing, demand, capacity shipments, gross margins are all improving. FCF growing materially, dividend raised, more buybacks
  * PO remains at $800 with minor changes to estimates

  
---  
| [FULL REPORT](https://rsch.baml.com/r?q=yLtrx2A!DiFCYNeD00HeWw__&e=felipe.monteiro%40capstone.com.br&h=XPoEUA)|     | [![](cid:bofaserpt13031832)](https://rsch.baml.com/r?q=yLtrx2A!DiFCYNeD00HeWw__&e=felipe.monteiro%40capstone.com.br&h=XPoEUA)  
---|---|---  
  
* * *  
  
---  
  
Late cycle capacity add concerns misplaced

WDC delivered another strong beat/raise. Mgmt. reiterated prior capex
commentary (modestly higher than 4.0-6.0% in F27/F28 in order to invest in
heads and media which manifest in EB growth in two years without adding unit
supply). We estimate demand is growing closer to 40% y/y and without investing
in heads and media, WDC would cap out in capacity at a much lower level.
Despite higher capex, FCF remains strong, as does focus on shareholder returns
(raised dividend 17% to $0.175/sh/qtr, and buybacks continue). Majority of
capex goes into head wafer investments (more steps in HAMR heads so needs to
add capacity to maintain throughput, and future drives will have more number
of platters/heads). Rest of capex for investing in glass substrate capacity
and dual actuators. Reiterate Buy on secular growth of the HDD market,
favorable supply/demand balance, strong EB growth driven by mix & further GM
upside.

Visibility now extends into 2031; HAMR ramp on track

For its top seven customers, WD now has demand visibility into 2031. Total
$/TB increased 28% y/y, further accelerating from high teens% y/y in F4Q26 and
HSD% y/y in F3Q26. EB shipments grew +7% q/q (+22% y/y) to 248 EB and we model
EB growth to accelerate through the rest of the qtrs of F27 as 40TB ePMR ramps
(to 30% of nearline shipments by end of F2Q and then to 50% by end of F3Q),
and as first gen HAMR finishes qualification and begins volume shipments in
C1H27. Then, 2nd gen HAMR qualification starts in C2H27 (5TB per platter, with
11 platters per drive).

Toshiba capacity adds not a threat; Cost downs lower n-t

Mgmt. does not see any capacity/unit adds by Toshiba as materially changing
industry supply/demand balance and industry share. Toshiba is dependent on 3rd
parties for heads and media so component capacity can be a constraint. WD's
cost downs will be less than 10% y/y in the near-term given multiple product
transitions.

Adjusting estimates, PO remains at $800

Our F27E revenue/EPS moves to $20.54bn/$23.80 (from $19.62bn/$22.37). Our PO
remains at $800 on 16x C28E EPS of $48.75 (prior $800 on 16x C28E EPS of
$49.67).

Growth](https://www.ubs.com/mas/rapi/ae654500ebbc721b269178f2bcf566df.png)
](https://neo.ubs.com/r/7/?id=h7f009bf7,dc35302,4bf87a5c&e=ZGlkPUFDNy1FLTIzMDkwNDU3OCZvZmZfaWQ9QUM3LUUtMTU5MTA2MDA4MiZtYT1ZNDY3ODUzNDk0OTc4NUE0NSZjYW1wX2lkPUVNOlVOS1c6MjAyNi0xMDoyMzpD&s=QywjNnR0AzGRkGhwdGk9hK7t6YpmPVcs4aXQj8_9040)  
Source: UBS estimates, Company reports; Note: C3Q26 values for STX are

| Summary Thoughts WDC once again posted solid results with guidance even a
touch better than our high-on-Street estimates as the company effectively
knows what it will ship each Q when it guides. Demand still significantly
exceeds supply and we have a lot of confidence in WDC's technology roadmap and
execution, but the narrative is starting to shift here in a way that we think
will continue to drive the multiple lower. Specifically, capex is moving
substantially higher and while the message on supply was somewhat muddled,
this seems likely to accelerate materially as well (closing the gap with STX
which is already growing supply above LT demand growth). This also comes amid
a more aggressive tack from Toshiba - which has a vastly inferior roadmap, but
we think is implicitly supported by hyperscale customers being willing to
sacrifice TCO for more supply (a development that we had been highlighting as
a possibility since May of this year
[here](https://neo.ubs.com/r/7/?id=h7f009bf7,dc35302,4bf87a5d&e=ZGlkPUFDNy1FLTIzMDkwNDU3OCZvZmZfaWQ9QUM3LUUtMTU5MTA2MDA4MyZtYT1ZNDY3ODUzNDk0OTc4NUE0NSZjYW1wX2lkPUVNOlVOS1c6MjAyNi0xMDoyMzpD&s=EXynr7kunVNfQWtHPaMV-
PcQkvwA3zj-4sgfrOhd0A0 "neo.ubs.com")). In the near/medium-term, there is
ample demand to soak up this supply but the market is more than ever trying to
risk-adjust the shape of demand on the other side of this cycle. We would
argue the risks here are much greater than memory because HDDs are sheer
capacity pools and memory is much harder to add supply and actually drives
inference token costs, which are therefore worthy of customer pre-payments.
Such is not the case for HDDs. Ultimately, it is true that the multiple here
has already compressed quite a bit, but we see no reason why HDD stocks should
command a premium to memory stocks like MU (in fact, maybe ultimately a
discount) so even though we walk numbers up once again (C2027 to ~$42 and
C2028 to ~$62), our PT actually comes down from $470 to $435 using the exact
same 7x multiple applied to C2028 EPS (for MU we use 7x C2029 but discount
back 1yr). Analysis/Key Highlights

  * Results: WDC reported Sept Q revenue of $4.38B, ~3% above UBSe and above the top of the guidance range. Bit shipments of 248EB were up ~7% Q/Q (~1% above UBSe), while ASP/TB of $17.67 was up ~9% Q/Q (~2% ahead of UBSe). Gross margin was 210bps above the top of the range and +10bps/+260bps above UBSe/Street, and OpM beat by a higher amount as opex was a little lighter. In all, EPS of $4.64 beat UBSe/Street by 6%/13%.
  * Guide: Management guided Dec Q revenue of $5.1B ± $100MM (1% above UBSe at the midpoint but well north of Street), GM of 60-61%, and OpM of ~53% resulting in EPS guidance of $5.80 ± $0.20, ~2% below UBSe at the midpoint. Of note, WDC has traditionally reported at the top of the range (Figure 3). The company was not specific as to the components of the guidance, but it did suggest that Y/Y increases in ASP/TB will increase in FQ2 and the guidance implies ASP/TB growing in a roughly similar range Q/Q to the +9% from FQ1. 
  * Pricing/Costdowns: EB shipments were in-line with expectations with pricing up ~28% Y/Y. WDC continues to highlight pricing moving higher on a Y/Y basis (its pricing trajectory has been steeper than STX's) but costdowns slowed to ~5% Y/Y and are expected to remain <10% due to some component cost inflation. WDC currently leads STX in avg capacity per drive but is ramping HAMR with its first 2 customers in C1H:27 and qualifying two additional customers. For C2H:27, it will qualify 2nd generation HAMR (5TB/platter on its 11 disk platform). In terms of mix, 40TB ePMR is ramping ahead of prior transitions and is expected to be ~30% of nearline EBs by FQ2 (Dec) and ~50% by FQ3 (Mar). 
  * Gross Margin: Incremental gross margin for Sept Q was above 80% Y/Y reflecting mix shift to higher capacity drives, execution and a favorable pricing environment. Coupled with 10% Y/Y costdowns over time, this could push margins even higher. We model gross margins exiting CY26E at 63%, exiting CY27E at 74%, and peaking in mid-CY28E at 77% before modeling our projected downcycle. The company expects HAMR to be gross margin accretive over time but initially gross margin neutral.
  * EB Growth/Capex: EB shipments increased 22% in Sept Y/Y, and WDC spoke more about the emergence of neoclouds as a new group of customers though it did not specify their relative size. As part of a substantial increase in capex (management suggested "a few" points above the high-end of the 4-6% LT model (e.g. ~8%) for the next 2yrs), and is suggesting an acceleration in EB supply that sounds like, in response to our question on the earnings call, it could ultimately approach the mid 30%s Y/Y growth that STX is currently putting up. Unit capacity is not growing and STX is spending money for heads, media and factory automation with part of this being due to HAMR carrying longer cycle times. Ergo, unit capacity is not growing, but this will still drive more EB supply. 
  * Customer Contracts: LTA discussions have extended to as far out as CY31, with outer year discussions centered around EB volumes rather than pricing. LTAs are structured such that base volumes are fixed at a certain price and upside volume is priced separately. Management has conviction that LTAs recontracting in the near term could see upside to pricing given the demand backdrop.
  * Capital Allocation: With FCF of $1.38B, in-line with UBSe and despite elevated capex, WDC ended the quarter in a net cash position of $0.5B. The company dedicated $1.0B to buybacks and increased the quarterly cash divided by 17%, while reiterating guidance of returning all FCF to shareholders through dividends and buybacks. WDC settled more than half of the $1.1B convert debt balance during the quarter. 

Read Across Demand remains strong and WDC's pricing theoretically opens more
headroom for STX. Overall, the demand commentary was also supportive for the
broad storage and memory complex. Valuation: PT $435 (from $470). We trim our
PT from $470 to $435, based on CY28E non-GAAP EPS of $61.67 (from $53.05)
applied to a target multiple of ~7x (from ~9x).

| Summary CoreWeave shares are -37% so far in October as investor confidence
in the broader “neo-cloud” AI infra stocks (Oracle included) has weakened
considerably. The shares of Microsoft and Amazon are actually UP over this
period, likely evidence of investors now adopting a far more defensive posture
in terms of AI infra exposure, a pivot that we generally agree with. In this
note we re-examine the CoreWeave credit story. Restoring confidence may be a
multi-quarter fix but we remain Buy-rated. Our View of CoreWeave The recent
share price weakness and widening of CDS/credit spreads have investors in
search of an explanation, a source of incremental fundamental deterioration.
Apart from rising rates (which absolutely do impact future funding costs), we
don’t see any fresh 'crack' in the story to warrant the sell-off, in fact the
demand, GPU pricing and 'up-the-stack' moves have been encouraging. Pinning
the sell-off on CoreWeave-specific factors is akin to arguing that a share
price decline must be a function of deteriorating fundamentals (sometimes it
is, often it isn’t). In our view, this is a reflection of a broader confidence
erosion in AI spending and stocks, expressed most acutely via the AI players
that are most capital-intensive, highly levered, FCF negative and rate-
sensitive. As such, this could take time to reverse. In this report we lay out
various CoreWeave funding scenarios (debt-heavy to debt-light) and note that
the broader UBS team is hosting an investor call on Monday at 11:00am ET to
address the AI debt financing market. Time to Play AI Defense We’re obviously
seeing a material recent pivot (deterioration) in AI stock sentiment, rooted
in weaker investor confidence in the durability of enterprise AI spend/demand
and the portion of spend ultimately captured by the LLM providers. In our
judgement, this sentiment shift is unlikely to reverse near-term and we too
are now being more defensive in our stock selection. This is one key reason
why we remain comfortable with and Buy-rated on the stocks of Microsoft and
Palantir – both are relatively model-agnostic (especially Palantir), chip-
agnostic, FCF positive with no/little need to access external funding sources
and with relatively diversified businesses (especially Microsoft).Valuation:
At just 2.2x revs and 3.8x adjusted EBITDA on 2027 estimates, at the very low
end of the range for the AI infra sub-sector, with heightened investor credit
concerns but no real deterioration in the business, we remain Buy-rated. A
restoration of confidence may take time though, and we’re trimming our price
target of $120 to $105, based on 2.8x our unchanged CY28 sales estimates,
still at the low end of the de-rated peer group.

# Investment Thesis, Valuation and Risks

### Western Digital (Overweight; Price Target: $650.00)

### Investment Thesis

We rate Western Digital shares Overweight driven primarily by the opportunity
for significant upside to consensus estimates, with the HDD industry
positioned to benefit from both strong demand stemming from hyperscaler capex
plans as well as pricing tailwinds. WDC is a powerhouse in storage, with its
portfolio comprising next-generation HDD solutions that are addressing the
growing data storage requirements at data center/cloud/AI infrastructure
customers. Near- and medium-term fundamentals continue to improve as the
industry is being disciplined in adding new capacity and focusing on
profitable growth.

### Valuation

We are increasing our December 2027 price target to $650 (vs. $600 prior),
based on valuing our 2028E EPS estimate at a mid-teens P/E multiple, which is
largely in-line with the target multiple for the key peer Seagate- and is
ahead of the historical multiple given robust HDD storage demand across data
centers.

### Risks to Rating and Price Target

faster-than-expected migration to flash-based storage driven by narrowing cost
differentials between HDDs and NAND, as well as greater progress on NAND
density – could present headwinds to our expectations for WDC shares.

| | WD just posted a strong, pricing-driven beat/raise, is accelerating rev growth to 70% Y/Y with ~80% incremental margins, has visibility into 2031 from its top 7 customers, and is returning 100% of FCF to shareholders. Capex comments were misinterpreted and we add clarity why below. Remain OW.   
---  
| | Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * Sept Q upside came from stronger EB growth and Price/EB growth, and both metrics should accelerate further throughout FY27. 
  * Dec Q EPS guide of $5.80 was 13% above our $5.25 forecast, which was 10% above Street ($4.84). Taking the T4Q avg EPS beat means Dec Q EPS likely goes $6.50+. 
  * Mgmt called out stronger demand, longer customer visibility, a broader customer base, and no change to industry fundamentals, countering recent headlines. 
  * Capex comments were misinterpreted. Yes, capex is ramping, but to support head/platter/substrate growth, not unit growth – mgmt previously communicated this. 
  * FY27/FY28 EPS moves 4-9% higher, even with conservative pricing forecasts. On unchanged 14x P/E, PT moves to $668. Remain OW. 

  
  
Clear confirmation of our Overweight thesis. The market continues to be fickle
(see our capex read below), but our conviction in the HDD bull case, as well
as WD's path to over $45 of EPS by FY28 has strengthened (FY28 bull case EPS
is $60+). What drives that conviction? A number of points that came up on
tonight's call: (1) HDD demand is stronger today than 3-6 months ago, and WD's
customer base is broadening out to neoclouds, frontier labs, and physical AI
companies, (2) WD expects Y/Y exabyte (EB) growth to accelerate through FY27
and FY28 and still fall short of customer demand, (3) WD's top 7 customers are
all now providing visibility out to 2030-2031 – 3 months ago WD talked about
customers starting to negotiate LTAs into CY29-CY31, (4) Price per EB growth
accelerated from +18% Y/Y in the June quarter to +28% Y/Y in the September
quarter, and December quarter guidance implies another period of price
acceleration with mgmt noting "_growth can accelerate for the next 3-4
quarters_ ", (5) 58% gross margins continue expanded by 350bps Q/Q, with 80%
incremental margins showing WD is nowhere close to peak, and (6) mgmt noted
they don't see any change to long-term fundamentals (supply, pricing, etc.)
for the industry and that the gap between supply and demand is not perishable,
with some customers reporting only 1 week of HDD inventory on hand today.

All told, things are only strengthening for WD. In fact, despite being 9%
ahead of Street EPS in the December quarter, WDC just guided 10%+ above our
estimates, and on average, has outperformed the midpoint of their EPS guidance
by 14% over the last 4 quarters – meaning when all is said and done December
quarter EPS could easily surpass $6+ vs. Consensus at $4.84. With shares in
the after-market now trading at 12.7x our new FY27 EPS (of $25.97) and 6.9x
our new FY28 EPS (of $47.73) WD is hovering around our "close your eyes and
buy" levels, and we remain OW-rated with a new $668 PT, or 102% upside, based
on 14x our new FY28 EPS. FWIW, we think tonight's report is also a clear
positive read-through to STX earnings next week, where we have gained
conviction in a pricing-driven beat/raise.

_What we learned from WDC's F1Q27 (September quarter) earnings call and
callback:_

(+) Price per bit growth should continue to accelerate through at least the
next 3-4 quarters. $/TB growth accelerated from the high-teens Y/Y in the June
quarter to +28% Y/Y in the September quarter (or $17.7/TB), and December
quarter guidance implies another step-up to >30% Y/Y growth. More importantly,
mgmt sees “further room” for Y/Y growth to accelerate over the next 3-4
quarters – consistent with our checks – driven by (1) existing LTAs include
periodic price increases, while expiring agreements are being renewed into a
better pricing environment, (2) exabytes outside LTAs are seeing particularly
strong pricing as we've noted, and (3) WDC continues to sell the value of TCO
savings as customers transition to higher-capacity drives. Notably, HAMR
should not disrupt this trajectory either, with mgmt explicitly noting that
HAMR will not be discounted vs. ePMR and will continue to be priced on a
premium $/TB basis. For reference, after growing 8% Q/Q in the September
quarter, we forecast nearline $/TB growth averaging just 6% Q/Q over the next
3 quarters, which we believe is very conservative. And yet we are still 25%
above Street EPS in FY27. If we were to assume Q/Q nearline $/TB growth very
modestly accelerates each of the next 3 quarters (to +9% Q/Q, then +10% Q/Q,
and then +11% Q/Q) – which would be more directionally consistent with our
checks – our FY27/FY28 EPS would be 9-16% higher than today, implying a
valuation closer to 6x P/E.

(=) The market misinterpreted mgmt's comments on capex – here's what you need
to know. Since spinning SNDK, WD has been consistent – they need to invest in
head/media/substrate capacity (plus automation tools) to support mix shift to
higher capacity 10-14 platter drives. Even as recently as September, when
referencing capex as a % of revenue, WD said "_...the next couple of years, we
might be actually slightly above that [4-6%] range, but when you look at it
over a 5 year period, it should be in or about that 4-6%_ ". So tonight's
capex comments – which drove the stock down 6.5% after-hours despite the
across the board beat/raise – were consistent with exactly what the company
has already told the market. And for anyone confused on platter growth vs.
unit growth, consider this fact – over the last 12 months, WD platter count
shipped has grown low-teens% Y/Y with minimal unit growth given mix shift to
higher capacity drives. And that growth doesn't even include mixing into the
11-14 platter 40-55TB ePMR and HAMR drives that are launching now and over the
next few years, which require even more platters/media/substrate due to a more
complex cycle process (hence the investments). Said differently, how else will
WD accelerate EB growth with minimal unit growth? Selling a greater mix of
higher capacity drives, which combine the areal density benefits of ePMR and
HAMR (i.e. more bits per platter) with increased platter (and head) count. If
anyone has any questions on this concept, please call us.

(=) Cost/TB declines not as robust in the short-term, but pricing upside
supports continued gross margin expansion. Over the last 4 quarters, WD has
averaged Y/Y cost per TB declines of 9% Y/Y, so we were surprised to see just
4.5% Y/Y cost/TB declines in the September quarter. But 2 factors worked
against WD – higher component costs (DRAM/NAND) and negative mix shift, with
non-nearline EBs growing 14% Q/Q vs. nearline EBs growing 7% Q/Q. However,
gross margins were able to expand 370bps Q/Q because pricing was much stronger
than expected. Both of these trends are expected to persist in the December
quarter, and into C1H27 – slower cost/TB declines between product transitions
but faster price/TB growth – which means gross margins should still expand
3-4pts Q/Q, on average. Once WD's newest ePMR drives reach 50%+ of nearline
EB's shipped and WD reduces reliance on certain commodities, we should see
cost per TB declines reaccelerate towards 10% Y/Y, which we conservatively
assume happens in the December '27 quarter.

(+) Up to 40TB ePMR tech is ramping in-line with expects, while the HAMR ramp
is now ahead of plan. WDC's latest 40TB ePMR platform is ramping in line with
expectations and customer adoption is progressing faster than prior product
transitions, which means these drives will represent ~30% of nearline EB
shipments in the December quarter and 50% of NL EB's in March. Meanwhile, WD's
HAMR progress is ahead of plan, with 2 hyperscalers finishing quals on
4TB/disk HAMR in C1Q27 and volume shipments commencing in C1H27, while 2
additional customers will begin qualifications in C1H27. WDs second-gen
5TB/disk HAMR qualifications will now start in C2H27, ahead of schedule.
Together, these product transitions give us increasing confidence that
September's +22% Y/Y EB growth represents a trough, with growth accelerating
over the next 6-8 quarters and supporting WDC's ability to deliver 25%+ long-
term Y/Y EB growth. [Read

L28:   * Revenue of $4.38 billion, up 55% year-over-year

L30:   * GAAP diluted EPS of $4.63; non-GAAP diluted EPS of $4.64

L33: SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 22, 2026-- Western Digital Corporation (Nasdaq: WDC) today reported fiscal first quarter 2027 financial results for the period ended October 2, 2026.
L34: “Fiscal 2027 is off to a strong start, with results exceeding expectations, driven by robust customer demand and disciplined execution. In our fiscal first quarter, revenue grew 55% year over year, non-GAAP gross and operating margins expanded to 58.1% and 49.1%, respectively, resulting in a 161% year-over-year increase in non-GAAP EPS.
L35: Reflecting our confidence in the business and our commitment to return capital to shareholders, we are raising our quarterly cash dividend by 17% to $0.175 per share,” said Irving Tan, CEO of WD. “We are executing well through our technology transitions to meet the growing demand for storage.
L36: As we deepen our customer relationships, broaden the customer base to new areas of the market, and extend our visibility into future demand, we are building an increasingly durable foundation for long-term value creation.”
